snippet.title: What's Hidden Under Antarctica?
snippet.description:
Something's hiding below the ice in Antarctica…. 
For optimistic science and tech stories, subscribe!

In 1970, a team of Soviet scientists started drilling. For 28 years, they kept going… until after nearly 4,000 meters… they suddenly stopped. Because they’d found something unimaginable: Liquid water. A secret lake, down below all this ice, that had been completely sealed off from the rest of the world for 15 million years. 

How? And… is there something alive in there? Creatures that have been evolving separately from the rest of the planet for 15 million years?

Scientists started searching for more of these secret lakes, and as they did, they realized there is way more going on under Antarctica than we ever thought.

I needed to know the truth about Earth’s most remote continent. So I've come all the way to Antarctica to show you what's really happening down below this ice. And exactly what they discovered when they finally broke inside…

Chapters: 
00:00 What’s hiding under Antarctica?
01:50 How thick is the ice in Antarctica?
2:30 What if you dig a hole into Antarctica? 
4:13 What’s inside a crevasse? 
4:56 How do we know what’s under the ice?
6:24 What if you go deeper?
07: 18 How old is the ice under Antarctica? 
10:33 Why are there lakes under Antarctica's ice?
13:31 How can we study the subglacial lakes?
15:19 Did we find new life under Antarctica? 
16:52 Can research in Antarctica help us find aliens in space? 
17:41 What don’t we know? 
18:12 What's next? 
18:22 :) 

Special thanks to Dr. Steven Chown, Rebecca Warne and all of the amazing guides from the White Desert Foundation leading Science Week .

You can find me on Instagram here: https://www.instagram.com/cleoabram 
On TikTok here: https://www.tiktok.com/@cleoabram 
Or on Twitter here: https://twitter.com/cleoabram 

Bio:
Cleo Abram is an Emmy-nominated independent video journalist. On her show, HUGE* If True, Cleo explores complex technology topics with rigor and optimism, helping her audience understand the world around them and see positive futures they can help build. Before going independent, Cleo was a video producer for Vox. She wrote and directed the Coding and Diamonds episodes of Vox’s Netflix show, Explained. She produced videos for Vox’s popular YouTube channel, was the host and senior producer of Vox’s first ever daily show, Answered, and was co-host and producer of Vox’s YouTube Originals show, Glad You Asked. 

Additional reading and watching:  
- History on the drilling into Lake Vostok: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/annals-of-glaciology/article/deep-drilling-at-vostok-station-antarctica-history-and-recent-events/8DA18E684DD19E80E7D02F2FBD2DFA26 
- Drilling into Lake Ellsworth: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/antarcticas-subglacial-lake-ellsworth-will-keep-its-secrets-for-now-75/ 
- WISSARD (Lake Whillans) drilling project: https://www.montana.edu/priscu/research/current/wissard-summary.html, https://astrobiology.nasa.gov/news/antarcticas-subglacial-lakes-support-prospects-for-life-on-icy-moons/ 
- SALSA (Lake Mercer) drilling project: https://today.ucsd.edu/story/researchers-extract-first-layered-lake-sediment-sample-from-subglacial-antarctica. 
- Beyond EPICA and Million year Ice Core Projects: https://www.beyondepica.eu/en/, https://www.antarctica.gov.au/science/climate-processes-and-change/antarctic-palaeoclimate/million-year-ice-core/
- Bedmap data from the British Antarctic Survey: https://bedmap.scar.org/ 
- The Polar Regions: https://nsidc.org/home, https://www.antarctica.gov.au/about-antarctica/ 
- Helen Fricker’s work + NASA’s ICESat tools: https://icesat-2.gsfc.nasa.gov/, https://today.ucsd.edu/story/uc-san-diego-led-science-team-selected-for-nasa-satellite-mission, https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1136897  
- John Priscu's research on the Lake Vostok’s accretion ice: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.286.5447.2141
- What's Hidden Under the Ice of Antarctica? (Real Life Lore): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KOnB47PyZJw 
- What’s Really Under Antarctica’s Ice (PBS Terra): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k7AzHDaTHHo 
- What’s Under Antarctica’s Ice? (SciShow): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xn9DWKSiqGQ 
- “The Lake at the Bottom of the World” (Documentary on Lake Mercer + SALSA Project): https://www.antarcticlakefilm.com/

Why do polar bears and penguins not get on?

localized.title: What's Hidden Under Antarctica?
localized.description:
Something's hiding below the ice in Antarctica…. 
For optimistic science and tech stories, subscribe!

In 1970, a team of Soviet scientists started drilling. For 28 years, they kept going… until after nearly 4,000 meters… they suddenly stopped. Because they’d found something unimaginable: Liquid water. A secret lake, down below all this ice, that had been completely sealed off from the rest of the world for 15 million years. 

How? And… is there something alive in there? Creatures that have been evolving separately from the rest of the planet for 15 million years?

Scientists started searching for more of these secret lakes, and as they did, they realized there is way more going on under Antarctica than we ever thought.

I needed to know the truth about Earth’s most remote continent. So I've come all the way to Antarctica to show you what's really happening down below this ice. And exactly what they discovered when they finally broke inside…

00:00 What’s hiding under Antarctica?
01:50 How thick is the ice in Antarctica?

15:19 Did we find new life under Antarctica? 
16:52 Can research in Antarctica help us find aliens in space? 
17:41 What don’t we know? 
18:12 What's next? 
18:22 :)

Bio:
Cleo Abram is an Emmy-nominated independent video journalist. Before going independent, Cleo was a video producer for Vox. She wrote and directed the Coding and Diamonds episodes of Vox’s Netflix show, Explained. She produced videos for Vox’s popular YouTube channel, was the host and senior producer of Vox’s first ever daily show, Answered, and was co-host and producer of Vox’s YouTube Originals show, Glad You Asked.

snippet.title: How One Tiny Country Rivals American Farming
snippet.description:
The Netherlands is the world’s second-largest agricultural exporter by value despite being only about the size of Maryland. Inside large greenhouses, farmers grow millions of tons of tomatoes and peppers with the help of bees, robots, and custom LED lights. The country's research hub, Wageningen University, has turned this innovation into a global model for farming. But now the industry faces rising energy prices, labor shortages, and a nitrogen pollution crisis. So how are the Dutch adapting, and can their model really feed the world?

snippet.title: Animals vs Engineers
snippet.description:
Welcome back to Camp CrunchLabs! Today, we’re learning about nature’s greatest engineers... animals! But will Zach King try to steal my new monkey friend? It’s not too late to join us for your least boring Summer ever! https://crunchlabs.com/CampAnimals

Each build-it-yourself STEM toy teaches the magic and fun of engineering principles and includes exclusive weekly videos like this one that accelerate your learning! Ready for Camp? Visit https://CrunchLabs.com/camp for more info.

A big thanks to our special guest​⁠ @ZachKing for joining me!

This Summer’s Challenges: 

First, a RUBE GOLDBERG MACHINE, but somewhere, it has to include WATER. A Rube Goldberg machine is basically a chain reaction you build, usually to accomplish a simple task, like turning on a light or feeding the dog. This summer, part of the chain reaction has to include water.

Next up is a SLO-MO VIDEO, but this one has to include one of the most important engineering devices ever invented… GOOGLY EYES. Now, for the record, they don't need to be official googly eyes with a lens - cutting out two white circles, and smaller black ones, will totally get the job done.

The final option, and again, you can totally do as many of these challenges as you want, is a REVERSE-VIDEO USING FOOD. There are a bunch of free phone apps that let you shoot a video and then play it back in reverse, so the challenge is to create something that looks cool in reverse and incorporates food in some way.

Parents: Complete the form on https://www.crunchlabs.com/pages/camp-crunchlabs-challenges-and-videos-2026-main to enter.

snippet.title: The Invisible Burden: Mental Load at Home | Dr. Judith Joseph with LG Global
snippet.description:
In my own research on high-functioning depression, I’ve tracked how these hidden burdens quietly erode our well-being. And recently, a new global study by @LGGlobal   perfectly proved the scale of this modern crisis. 

The data reveals that people spend nearly a quarter of the year — about 87 days — burdened by this invisible mental load. On average, our minds are interrupted 27 times a day by routine demands. 

This means your brain is never truly off the clock; it is silently working, even when you think you are resting.

In our professional lives, we naturally use intelligent technology and AI to save our energy and time. We can apply that same wisdom to our homes. This is why I deeply appreciate how @LGGlobal   is bringing this issue to light. 

While most of the world only focuses on productivity, they are addressing the root of mental load. True well-being in the AI era means using intelligent technology to ease these everyday cognitive demands.  By letting technology handle the routine management of the home, your mind can finally find a moment to truly rest.

The findings from both my clinical work and global research reveal a beautiful human truth: when that weight is lifted, people don’t reach for greater productivity. They just want the freedom to be spontaneous — to get lost in a book or spend unplanned time with loved ones.

Reducing your mental load is about freeing up the psychological capital required to reclaim your joy, spontaneity, and human connection. Ultimately, it is these meaningful moments that truly make life good.

So, as you come home today, I hope you take that first step to free up your mind for the stuff that matters. Thank you for watching and take care of your mind.

snippet.title: Generating novel scientific hypotheses with Co-Scientist
snippet.description:
In an era of information overload, the search for transformative scientific ideas has become a significant bottleneck for progress.

Every great scientific breakthrough begins with a single, transformative idea. The spark of discovery relies on a researcher's ability to connect disparate facts and formulate the right hypothesis to test.

We believe AI can help dramatically accelerate the pace of breakthroughs by serving as a dedicated partner in the generation and refinement of breakthrough scientific hypotheses. That’s why we’ve developed Co-Scientist, a Gemini-based multi-agent AI system that iteratively generates, debates, and evolves novel hypotheses for complex scientific problems.

Read the Nature paper: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10644-y and learn more at labs.google/science

snippet.title: Can a Camera on Every Corner Make Us Safer? | Garrett Langley | TED
snippet.description:
Garrett Langley founded Flock because of a basic frustration: it was too easy to get away with crime in the US. His solution — a network of license plate readers, cameras, drones and audio sensors — has changed how police departments investigate crime, while also raising urgent questions about safety, surveillance and privacy. In this talk, Langley addresses the controversy around this widely debated technology and makes the case for why it will make the world safer. (Followed by a Q&A with TED Chairman Chris Anderson and a note from TED guest curator Bilawal Sidhu) (Recorded at TED2026 on April 14, 2026)

localized.description:

snippet.title: Man Builds The MOST SECRET Cabin In The World | Start To Finish By @PolissyaBushcraft
snippet.description:
In this project, Michael’s goal is not to build a cabin that rises above the trees, but a warm, hidden dugout buried beneath the forest floor, concealed under the remains of an old stump. 

What looks from the outside like a natural piece of woodland decay slowly becomes something far more surprising: a secret underground shelter shaped by hand, earth, clay, bark, moss, fire, and instinct.

As you’ll see, this is bushcraft at its most immersive. Michael digs into the ground, carves the interior, builds a ladder, forms a clay hearth, creates a smoke outlet disguised as part of the stump, lays a straw bed, covers the roof with logs and moss, and hides the entrance so carefully that the shelter begins to blend back into the forest. 

Suddenly, the old stump becomes camouflage. And when night falls, the small hidden room glows with firelight, turning a hole in the ground into a warm survival refuge.

Polissya Bushcraft

snippet.title: The Massive Machine Hidden in the Deep Ocean
snippet.description:
Off the coast of Sicily, there’s a massive underwater machine. It looks like a forest of floating spheres…

And on the surface, hidden in an abandoned winery, a computer watches them and waits. And in 2023, they saw something…

Something WAY smaller than an electron tore through that forest, setting off a signal nearly 30x more powerful than anything like it we’ve seen before, which means something HUGE must have happened way out in space.

This crazy experiment is not alone! Down in Antarctica, buried deep in the ice, are over 5000 more of these mysterious spheres. 

Together, these two machines – called KM3net and Ice Cube – are part of a massive global effort to give us a brand new way to find and look inside the biggest, most extreme, cosmic events in our universe.

But to do it, they need to catch the most elusive particle in all of physics.

And in this episode of HUGE* If True, we’re going to show you how…

This episode was made possible by AT&T, the official connectivity partner of HUGE* If True.

00:00 What's the machine hidden under the sea?
02:40 What is a neutrino? 
03:24 How do we know what's out in the universe? 
06:06 How do you catch a neutrino? 
08:08 Why can’t we see neutrinos? 
11:42 How do you know you’ve detected a neutrino? 
12:27 What’s hiding underneath Antarctica? 
13:08 What have we discovered with neutrinos? 
14:44 What don’t we know yet?

15:44 :)

snippet.title: The Sun Is Weirder Than You Think
snippet.description:
If you dove into the sun, the first layer you’d hit is hot enough to make diamonds BOIL. 

Right now we’re in a golden age of new solar science. For the first time, we’re getting close-up pictures of the Sun like we’ve never seen. Sending probes into its atmosphere. And revealing secrets about our star we never thought possible… 

Trust me, after this video, you’ll never look up at the sun the same way. 

So let me take you on a journey… INTO THE SUN.

This episode was made possible by AT&T, the official connectivity partner of HUGE* If True. 

Chapters 
00:00 What happens if you dive into the Sun?
01:11 Is the Sun a giant ball of fire?
03:16 How far away is the Sun?
06:17 What does the Sun sound like?
07:13 Are solar storms dangerous?
09:14 What is the surface of the Sun like?
11:31 Why does light get trapped inside the Sun?
12:51 How do we know what's inside the Sun?
14:20 How does the Sun make energy?
15:39 How big is the Sun?
16:01 When will the Sun die?

snippet.title: Something’s Happening to the Ozone Hole
snippet.description:
This is ANTARCTICA. And in 1985, it became the center of a global crisis… 

Directly over Antarctica, high up in the stratosphere was a massive hole. And if we hadn’t done anything about it, today, we’d be living in an alternate world. 

By now, a hole would be forming over the North Pole as well. By 2040, the “hole” would be over the entire planet. By 2065, skin cancer rates would be soaring. Kids wouldn’t play outside much anymore… 

But that’s NOT the world we’re living in! In fact, you’ve probably stopped hearing this story altogether.
That wasn’t by accident. It was a choice. Two choices, both of which dramatically changed the course of human history for the better.

So let me show you how that happened and what's about to happen next. Because it turns out, the little sliver at the bottom of the map is actually the center of everything/our whole planet.  

And you need to see this now, because scientists say we need to make the next big choice. 

Visit http://mercury.com to join over 300 thousand entrepreneurs who love Mercury. Mercury is a financial technology company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

snippet.title: The $1 Trillion Problem Diamonds Can Solve
snippet.description:
Most people think of diamonds as expensive jewelry, or maybe as super-hard drills. But everyone’s missing the coolest story here… 

We’ve built giant machines that can recreate the conditions inside our planet. And found new ways to make diamonds way cheaper, now unlocking the hidden potential of this super material. 

People are sending diamonds into space, adding them to massive computers, and using them to help solve one of the biggest technological problems we’re about to face.

This is about pushing the limits of material science to benefit all of us. So in this video, we’re getting rare access inside a lab where they make diamonds to see how they actually do it… 

And we’re gonna shrink down inside your computer to show you why diamonds are not what you think.

Chapters: 
00:00 Diamonds are not what you think
01:38 Where do natural diamonds come from?
02:17 Why are diamonds so hard?
03:48 What's a diamond's secret superpower?
05:09 Why does my computer get so hot? 
05:50 How small is a transistor?   
06:43 What's the limitation of transistors? 
10:32 Who grew a diamond first? 
11:49 How do you grow a diamond now? 
13:39 Are natural diamonds better than lab grown?
14:24 How could diamonds be used next?
15:21 Why are engineers so excited about diamonds?
16:28 :)

snippet.title: Famous Paleontologist Dishes on Dinosaur Extinction
snippet.description:
If dinosaurs could be wiped out in a geological instant, what does that say about us?

Sixty-six million years ago, a single asteroid ended the age of dinosaurs and triggered one of the most catastrophic mass extinction events in Earth’s history.

Learn all about what happened and what happened next in this new video from Colossal Biosciences, the de-extinction company.

Dr. Kenneth Lacovara, a renowned paleontologist, geologist, and member of the Colossal Scientific Advisory Board, walks you through what really happened during the fifth mass extinction event. How big was the asteroid? What did the Chicxulub impact crater reveal? How fast did the dinosaurs die? And what were those final hours like on a planet hit by a magnitude 10 to 11 global earthquake and an atmosphere heated to pizza-oven-level temperatures?

 We explore the T. rex experience, the science behind impact winter, and the drilling projects that helped reconstruct the timeline of extinction.

Then we zoom out. What if the asteroid had missed? Would non-avian dinosaurs still dominate Earth? Would mammals ever have risen? Would humans even exist? 🤯

Using the cosmic calendar analogy, we compress 4.5 billion years of Earth’s history into a single year and reveal just how recently dinosaurs went extinct and how shockingly new Homo sapiens really are.

This isn’t just a story about dinosaurs. It’s a story about existence, evolution, adaptive radiation, and how one mass extinction event reshaped the trajectory of life on Earth.

Dr. Lacovara is also the Founding Executive Director at the Edelman Field Museum, make sure to give them a follow and visit the museum if you have access: https://www.efm.org/

0:00 - Intro
0:44 - The End of the Dinosaurs (Title)
0:47 - When the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs hit Earth, what were the apex predators? What else was walking the Earth during that time?
1:24 - After the asteroid hit the Earth, how long do we believe it took to kill off the dinosaurs? Do we have any idea what those final days and months were like?
2:47 - How do we know dreadnoughtus wasn't afraid of the crushing burden of responsibility for the consequences of its actions?
3:22 - If that asteroid hadn't hit Earth, what would the world be like today? Would there still be dinosaurs?
4:38 - Is it true that you are actually a character being played by Bruce Willis?
4:52 - What’s the shortest version you could tell of the story of life on Earth?

Welcome to The End of the Dinosaurs.

About Colossal Biosciences:

MAKING EXTINCTION A THING OF THE PAST.

Colossal is a breakthrough bioscience and genetic engineering company that builds radical new technologies to advance the field of genomics. Colossal Biosciences creates disruptive technologies for extinct species restoration, critically endangered species protection and the repopulation of critical ecosystems that support the continuation of life on Earth. The company is the first to apply CRISPR technology for the purposes of species de-extinction. Colossal is accepting humanity’s duty to restore Earth to a healthier state, while also solving for the future economies and biological necessities of the human condition through cutting-edge science and technologies.

snippet.description:

snippet.title: Artemis II to the Moon: Launch to Splashdown (NASA Mission Animation)
snippet.description:
The Artemis II mission, slated to launch early 2026, will fly four astronauts around the Moon. This mission will last for about 10 days and will be the first crewed test flight of the Space Launch System rocket, the Orion spacecraft, and the Exploration Ground Systems at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center Florida needed to support them. 

Not only will this mission be the first time in over 50 years that human beings have seen the Moon close-up, Artemis II will also prepare us for future human landings on the Moon starting with the Artemis III mission and help prepare for future missions to Mars.

To learn more about the Artemis II mission, visit: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/
Download this video: https://images.nasa.gov/details/NHQ_2025_0307_Artemis%20II%20to%20the%20Moon%20Launch%20to%20Splashdown%20%28NASA%20Mission%20Animation%29

Credit: NASA

snippet.title: He Left SpaceX to Change How Homes Are Built
snippet.description:
America's lumber supply is one trade dispute or one bad storm away from sending home construction costs surging by thousands of dollars. A startup in North Carolina thinks grass is the fix.

*Find a system everyone depends on it and own a layer of it:* https://clickhubspot.com/d2nt

Plantd was founded by former SpaceX engineers who set out to replace oriented strand board — the structural panels that wrap the walls, floors, and roofs of nearly every home built in the US — with panels made from a perennial grass that grows six inches a day and can be harvested twice a year. Their boards are independently certified for use in all 50 states and, according to their own testing, are 1.5x stronger and 2x more moisture resistant than standard softwood OSB. D.R. Horton, the largest homebuilder in the country, has already ordered 10 million of them.

The catch: at 250k panels a year, that order alone would take 40 years to fill. Noelle went to Oxford, NC to see how Plantd plans to get there — and whether its bet on grass can hold up against one of America's oldest industries.

1:44 – Why Grass, Why North Carolina?
2:32 – From SpaceX to Solving Housing
2:59 – The Spark: Talking to Builders About OSB
5:29 – What OSB Is (and Plantd’s First Big Break)

6:02 – The Modular Mill “Moat” 
7:02 – Inside Plantd’s Mini Mill: Turning Grass into Panels
10:12 – How Lumber Got So Volatile (Storms, Tariffs, and Baby Trees)

snippet.title: QUANTAS BEXIGAS precisam para LEVANTAR uma PESSOA? feat. Giuliana Mafra #NosTestamos
snippet.description:
Quantas bexigas de gás hélio seriam necessárias para levantar uma pessoa de verdade?
A resposta não é nada óbvia — e envolve muito mais do que só sair enchendo bexiga.

Neste vídeo, o Iberê e a Giuliana Mafra colocam a física à prova: testam linhas, mosquetões, tipos de bexiga, força de tração, vazamento de hélio, segurança e fazem contas reais pra descobrir se essa ideia maluca é possível de verdade.

Não é mágica.
É densidade, empuxo, volume… e muita curiosidade científica.

snippet.title: Oktane Keynote Recap: Okta CEO Todd McKinnon on Agent SSO, Cross App Access, and AI Agent Security
snippet.description:
At the biggest Oktane ever, Okta CEO & Co-Founder Todd McKinnon addresses the defining technical challenge of the agentic age: balancing rapid AI innovation with enterprise security. Today, organizations face a false choice—either lock down AI agents and sacrifice innovation, or give them full access and assume immense risk.   

The solution is achieving total visibility and control. In this keynote highlight, Todd outlines Okta’s strategic roadmap to secure every AI agent across three core pillars: The Blueprint Alliance, Agent SSO, and Okta for AI Agents.   

5 Key Takeaways:

• The Blueprint Alliance: Okta has partnered with industry leaders across every layer of the tech stack to form a multi-vendor reference architecture that answers four critical questions: Where are my agents? What can they do? What are they doing? How do I respond?   

• Agent SSO Included in Core Plans: Agent SSO brings the seamless, centralized user experience of traditional single sign-on to AI agents, included across all Okta products.   

• Cross App Access (XAA) Open Standard: Agent SSO is built on Cross App Access (XAA), an open standard that replaces user consent prompts with predefined enterprise identity provider policies.   

• Shadow AI Discovery & Agent Gateway: Okta for AI Agents introduces endpoint discovery integrated with CrowdStrike and Okta Verify, alongside Agent Gateway—a virtual MCP server providing centralized authorization and a kill switch.   

• Heterogeneous & Commerce Support: Okta for AI Agents now supports third-party identity providers (IdPs), while Auth0 powers Auth for UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) for seamless, secure shopping within platforms like Google Gemini.   

Join the Blueprint Alliance and help set the open standard for the secure agentic future.   

📌 Resources & Links:

Learn more about Okta for AI Agents: https://www.okta.com/products/govern-ai-agent-identity/

Download the Blueprint for the Secure Agentic Enterprise: https://blueprintalliance.ai/

Explore Agent SSO & Cross App Access (XAA): https://www.okta.com/resources/datasheets/agent-sso/

0:25 - The False Choice: Locking Down AI vs. Assuming Risk

3:31 - Okta for AI Agents Velocity & Feature Announcements   
3:57 - Shadow AI Discovery, Agent Gateway & 3rd Party IdPs

snippet.title: Você não imagina como o LEITE EM PÓ é feito! O processo vai ter surpreender
snippet.description:
Você já se perguntou como é feito o leite em pó que você compra no mercado?

No vídeo de hoje, o Fábrica de Tudo mostra todo o processo industrial do leite em pó — desde a ordenha automatizada nas fazendas até a secagem por spray dryer e o empacotamento final.
Um conteúdo técnico e curioso, que revela como a indústria consegue transformar um líquido perecível em um produto leve, nutritivo e de longa duração.

🔍 O que você vai ver neste vídeo:

Como funciona a ordenha moderna e automatizada
A importância da pasteurização e da padronização da gordura
Como o spray dryer transforma leite líquido em pó
Quantos litros de leite são necessários para produzir 1kg de leite em pó
Por que o leite em pó gruda no céu da boca
As etapas de peneiramento, resfriamento e embalagem
E as diferenças entre os tipos de leite em pó: integral, desnatado, semidesnatado, instantâneo, fortificado e sem lactose

snippet.title: ACIDENTE RADIOATIVO em GOIÂNIA: O que FALTOU EXPLICAR
snippet.description:
Um dos acidentes mais graves da história aconteceu no Brasil, e começou de um jeito que ninguém poderia imaginar. Neste vídeo, a gente volta para Goiânia, em 1987, para entender como um material aparentemente inofensivo acabou se espalhando, afetando centenas de pessoas e gerando uma operação gigantesca para conter os danos.

👉 O que é o Césio-137?
👉 Por que ele pode ser tão perigoso?
👉 E como algo invisível conseguiu causar um impacto tão grande?

Ao longo da história, você vai entender não só o que aconteceu, mas também como a ciência e as equipes envolvidas conseguiram lidar com uma situação extremamente complexa.

Prepare-se: essa é uma daquelas histórias reais que parecem ficção, mas não são.

snippet.title: Dá ruim ficar ACENDENDO e APAGANDO a LUZ? Nós testamos!
snippet.description:
Compre todos os LIVROS e JOGOS do Manual do Mundo em: https://amzn.to/3AAc6L8

Sabe quando você ficava brincando de acender e apagar a luz rapidinho e alguém dizia: "Para com isso, vai queimar a lâmpada"? A gente resolveu levar essa brincadeira a sério e fez um dos testes mais longos da história do Manual do Mundo. Usamos um sistema automático que ficou ligando e desligando várias lâmpadas por vários dias seguidos. Testamos lâmpadas incandescentes e de LED para ver se tinha diferença e fizemos elas acenderem e apagarem milhões de vezes. Sim, milhões! Será que os pais estavam certos?

snippet.title: Gas Station Egg Salad Sandwich Ruins A Mom's Life
snippet.description:
Patient GM by Laura Galvan. PA and Doctor by Brandon Galvan. Review: Dr Katherine Johns
In-depth channel: @HemeReview 
Secret channel: @BigEmus 

Music by @Lifeformed ► https://lifeformed.bandcamp.com
Other music inspired by R Prince (RIP), performed by Chubbyemu

Chubbyemu Medical Cases (YouTube Podcast Playlist) https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL26HeTCO57qdRdf7qEivfDF_PvyZS40I4

Chubbyemu Medical Cases (YouTube Show) https://www.youtube.com/show/VLPL26HeTCO57qcwwwfagzFQfwh04PhNzJ0D?sbp=KgtobXV1aW4zQWFWc0AB

Medicine ► https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL26HeTCO57qcMQB6CrU6QRzEi9tt9l1FI

Thumbnail original image taken by Prof Rebecca Saxe

These cases are patients who I, or my colleagues have seen. They are de-identified and many instances have been presented in more depth in an academic setting. These videos are not individual medical advice and are for general educational purposes only.  I do not give medical advice over the internet.

Recalls and outbreaks are different situations but can overlap. Most (not all) recalls happening now are from the company who makes the product, and often (but not always) done before anyone gets sick. Sometimes it's a genuine mistake in the company. Other times it's some mix of bad leadership and management, poor competence, and no regard for social responsibility. Outbreaks are "later" in time, meaning the contaminated products have already been out for a while, people have interacted with and consumed them, and people have gotten sick from food poisoning and the like, and now the local and federal agencies have to investigate. Recall situations are easier to control. Outbreaks, like the cyclospora one, are much more unpredictable and harder to control. In this environment, you can control what you pay attention to, and it is best to see the current recalls and alerts from FDA and CDC. The fact that we're still hearing about them means the system isn't completely turned to mush right now, despite the ongoing narratives. But you still have to do what you need to, to protect yourself.

snippet.title: Inference at Scale: The New Frontier for AI Infrastructure and ROI
snippet.description:
AI factories are the new industrial engines — and their profitability hinges on how efficiently they generate intelligence.

The rise of AI reasoning models — capable of multi-step logic, complex decision-making, and real-time responsiveness — is redefining what’s possible with AI. But it also comes with a cost: these models demand significantly more compute during inference than their predecessors. That means the infrastructure powering them must become radically more efficient.

In this video, we break down the critical balance between performance, power, and profitability in modern AI inference. As reasoning models generate more valuable tokens and power more intelligent services, AI factories must maximize what they can produce within fixed power budgets. These factories are power-constrained by design — so performance per watt isn’t just a benchmark. It’s the foundation of profitability.

But achieving optimal performance per watt isn’t only about chip efficiency. It’s also about how intelligently inference is deployed. Balancing maximum throughput and minimum latency are the critical levers for growing gross profit from the same capital equipment — especially as reasoning models push computational demands to new heights.

If you're leading infrastructure strategy, scaling AI services, or investing in the next wave of intelligent production, this is your roadmap. Watch how smarter inference and full-stack infrastructure drive the economics of tomorrow’s AI factories.

Learn more: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/ai/inference/?ncid=so-yout-696353 and https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ai-factory-inference-optimization/?ncid=so-yout-777041

snippet.title: DESMONTAMOS uma ARMA DE CHOQUE! #OQueTemDentro
snippet.description:
Hoje a gente investiga como funciona uma arma de choque! Será que esse equipamento é perigoso mesmo? Pode machucar alguém de verdade? É permitido por lei ter uma dessas no Brasil? Iberê desmonta o aparelho, testa em vários objetos — inclusive em uma perna de rã — e ainda explica os princípios de física e química por trás da faísca elétrica.
No meio do vídeo, rola até uma experiência estilo Galvani para ver se o choque consegue ativar músculos. E, claro, alguém (voluntário!) leva um baita choque no final pra testar na prática o efeito no corpo humano. Além de entender os componentes internos — como capacitores, bobinas e a transformação de corrente — você também vai aprender por que essa faísca é, na verdade, plasma, e como ela se parece com um raio em miniatura. Mas atenção: apesar de não ser proibido, esse tipo de dispositivo é perigoso e não é brinquedo!

snippet.title: COMO é FEITO o ESTALINHO? #Boravê
snippet.description:
Como fabricar um produto que explode quando bate no chão, sem explodir a fábrica inteira?

Visitamos a maior fabricante de estalinhos das Américas para acompanhar todas as etapas da produção e descobrir o que realmente existe dentro da famosa biribinha.

Ao longo do processo, encontramos química, engenharia, controle de umidade, máquinas de alta precisão e descobrimos por que esse pequeno estalo funciona de um jeito completamente diferente do que muita gente imagina.

What did Earth look like a billion years ago? Before Pangea, before dinosaurs—even before oxygen filled the air—continents were on the move. In this Howtown episode, we travel billions of years into the past to explore a groundbreaking new plate tectonic model. Discover how scientists trace ancient continents using zircon crystals, magnetic minerals, glacial scars, and more. From massive dike swarms to lost supercontinents like Rodinia and Nuna, we unravel the clues that reveal Earth's epic tectonic story.

🔬 Featuring: Paleomagnetism, zircon dating, cratons, and the surprising history of plate tectonics
🛰️ NASA satellites, moon rocks, and ancient Canadian crust
👥 With special guest Joe Hanson (@besmart )

Watch Joe's companion video on zircon dating here → https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c4GRLFuTyQY

Key Source: Earth’s tectonic and plate boundary evolution over 1.8 billion years, Xianzhi Cao et al (2024) https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1674987124001464

A  história do macarrão instantâneo e por que ele é chamado de  "miojo"

O processo de laminação, corte e ondulação da massa

** O QUE É CIÁTICA?
"Ciática" é dor, formigamento, dormência, ou queimação que começa na parte inferior das costas ou glúteo e desce pela parte de trás da perna. É a apresentação característica da irritação no nervo ciático.

** O QUE CAUSA CIÁTICA
Essas sensações de dormência, formigamento ou dor são o resultado de uma irritação no nervo ciático. Seja uma hérnia de disco nas costas, suas vértebras ou um músculo - qualquer coisa que pressione e pressione o nervo ciático pode resultar em sintomas do nervo ciático.

** MELHOR EXERCÍCIO PARA TRATAR CIÁTICA
Agora, dependendo da causa exata da sua ciática, a progressão do exercício de tratamento parece um pouco diferente. Por exemplo, há certos exercícios que eu daria a um paciente com ciática de um disco protuberante que eu absolutamente NÃO recomendaria para alguém com ciática de estenose ou doença degenerativa do disco (é crucial que você consulte um profissional de saúde local para exercícios específicos para seu diagnóstico exclusivo).

snippet.title: Incredible footage shows how owl uses sound to hunt under snow
snippet.description:
In a Manitoba forest, a great grey owl sits atop a spindly branch. Then, wings outstretched, it descends from its perch, gliding over the blanket of snow. Specially adapted feathers allow it to do so in dead silence. After all, it wouldn't be good to drown out the noise of your own food. 

In this clip from Hunters and Hunted, the first episode of Secret World of Sound, a series from The Nature of Things, we follow the great grey owl as it hunts for food to sustain it through the winter. 
Watch the full episode: https://youtu.be/BYjVVBFgl3c
Also streaming on CBC Gem.

snippet.description:
Confira mais sobre jeans no site da Levi’s:  https://bit.ly/43UQMv1

Você já parou pra pensar como é feita uma calça jeans? A gente foi até uma fábrica da Levi’s para descobrir o que acontece desde o tecido até a peça pronta para chegar na loja.

Descubra como os jeans ganham cor, os cortes precisos, a costura reforçada e até os efeitos de desgaste que parecem naturais, mas são feitos com MUITA tecnologia!

snippet.title: O QUE TEM DENTRO da BOLA oficial da COPA 2026?
snippet.description:

snippet.title: The World’s Largest Electric Aircraft Just Flew
snippet.description:
Heart Aerospace (YC W19) just flew the largest electric airplane ever flown — a 100-foot wingspan, a takeoff weight of 25,000 pounds, and $5 of electricity to get it off the ground.

In this episode of Hard Tech, YC's Gustaf Alströmer visits Heart's pilot plant in LA and sits down with co-founder and CEO Anders Forslund to find out how they went from a 3D-printed model to a full-scale electric aircraft in seven years, why the jet engine has left short flights behind, and what cheap electric flight could unlock for the future of regional air travel.

https://www.heartaerospace.com

snippet.title: We heard you: the new Framework Laptop 13 Pro.
snippet.description:
You asked… we listened.

The Framework Laptop 13 Pro is a ground-up redesign of Framework Laptop 13, built from seven generations of iteration and feedback. It features 20 hours of battery life and a 74Wh battery, Intel® Core™ Ultra ​Series 3 Processors​, and LPCAMM2 modular LPDDR5x memory. We also introduced a custom 13.5” high-resolution touchscreen display, an improved haptic touchpad, and a new CNC aluminum chassis.

Framework Laptop 13 Pro was designed for Linux from the start, with broad distro support, upstream contributions, and for the first time, Ubuntu certified pre-built configurations. 

The Framework Laptop 13 Pro Mainboard is backwards compatible with all previous Framework Laptop 13 systems, enabling existing owners to upgrade to the latest generation. Watch our upgrade video here to learn more: https://youtu.be/JSxgCEpkiKM

Pre-orders are open now at https://frame.work

snippet.title: Como é FEITO um CAPACETE? #Boravê
snippet.description:
Hoje o Manual do Mundo foi ao interior de São Paulo para mostrar de perto como nasce um capacete de moto — desde o projeto no computador até os testes brutais de segurança. 

Você vai conhecer o processo de injeção do casco, a fabricação dos forros internos, as etapas de pintura e personalização e, o mais impressionante: o laboratório onde os capacetes são colocados à prova em situações extremas. Tem impacto, perfuração, queda, compressão e tudo o que for preciso para garantir que o capacete faça o que promete.

Mas será que ele realmente aguenta um acidente de verdade?
E o que acontece com ele por dentro depois de uma queda?
O vídeo termina com uma surpresa emocionante — e um alerta importante para quem anda de moto.

snippet.title: O QUE É esse TAL de EL NIÑO? ENTENDA TUDO sobre o FENÔMENO!
snippet.description:
O El Niño está entre os fenômenos climáticos mais conhecidos do planeta, mas você sabe o que realmente acontece no oceano para ele surgir? E como uma mudança na temperatura das águas do Pacífico consegue afetar lugares que estão a milhares de quilômetros dali?

Neste vídeo do Manual do Mundo, voltamos quase 500 anos para descobrir de onde veio o nome El Niño e fazemos uma experiência para visualizar o que acontece com as águas do Oceano Pacífico. Com a ajuda de mapas e das explicações de Gilvan Sampaio, pesquisador do INPE, entendemos o papel dos ventos alísios e por que uma alteração nesse enorme sistema pode provocar consequências tão distantes.

Também investigamos o que significa falar em um “Super El Niño”, como fenômenos naturais podem se combinar com outras mudanças no clima e o que tudo isso pode representar para o Brasil. E, para completar, explicamos o que é La Niña e por que os dois fenômenos estão tão relacionados.

snippet.title: What The Super El Niño Will Do To Our Weather In Coming Weeks
snippet.description:
A super El Niño is building in the Pacific, and its effects have already started spreading across the world.

NOAA declared El Niño on June 11, and in the weeks since, the forecasts have only gotten stronger. There's now an 81% chance this becomes a very strong El Niño between October and December, ranking among the largest events since records began in 1950, with the European model projecting ocean temperatures more than 3°C above average.

snippet.title: The AI Arsenal That Could Stop World War III | Palmer Luckey | TED
snippet.description:
AI in warfare is no longer hypothetical; it's inevitable, says Palmer Luckey, an inventor and founder of the defense technology company Anduril Industries. He takes us inside the high-tech arms race to build AI-powered weapons, "killer robots" and autonomous fighter jets at scale — and makes the counterintuitive case for why this may be the surest path to deterrence and lasting peace. (Followed by Q&A with technologist Bilawal Sidhu) (Recorded at TED2025 on April 8, 2025)

snippet.title: How a 3,000-Year-Old Obsession Built the Suez Canal
snippet.description:
For over two thousand years, the world’s greatest empires tried—and failed—to cut a water shortcut through the blistering Egyptian desert.

From Pharaoh Necho’s deadly ancient trenches and royal superstitions to Napoleon’s infamous survey blunder claiming one sea would flood the other, this strip of sand remained an impossible dream. It wasn't resolved by royal decrees, but by an arrogant French diplomat's gamble and the nineteenth century's first steam-powered iron monsters chewing through millions of tons of desert rock.

In this video, we trace the full, brutal history of the Suez Canal: the ancient dead ends, the horrific human cost of manual labor, the industrial revolution that finally forced the two seas together, and the modern geopolitical choke point it has become today.

What do you think is next for the world's most critical maritime bottleneck as mega-ships push it to its absolute limits? Share your thoughts below!

snippet.title: The Next Big Earthquake Could Sink Parts of the Pacific Northwest | NOVA | PBS
snippet.description:
A massive earthquake along the Cascadia Subduction Zone could unleash a tsunami and sink parts of the Pacific Northwest by several feet. 

A 2025 study suggests that when the next "Big One" hits, coastal land could sink by up to 6 feet. That sudden drop could instantly double the number of people, homes, and roads exposed to flooding.

snippet.title: This cell just changed biology
snippet.description:

snippet.title: QUANTOS GRÃOS tem no SACO DE ARROZ? Nós contamos!
snippet.description:
Quantos grãos de arroz será que tem em um saco de 5 kg? 🤔
A gente resolveu descobrir isso na prática — e de um jeito bem mais científico do que contar grão por grão (apesar de a gente ter feito isso também 😅).
Usamos métodos diferentes para estimar o número de grãos: pesando alguns grãos e fazendo uma regra de três, medindo o volume com potinhos, usando estatística com grãos marcados e espalhando no chão e medindo por área. E no fim ainda teve contagem com inteligência artificial e uma contagem manual com ajuda dos alunos da Mauá! Será que as estimativas chegam perto do número real?

snippet.title: Como o Japão construiu um muro gigante de 400 km contra tsunamis que impressiona o mundo
snippet.description: Após o devastador tsunami de 2011 que causou mais de 18.000 mortes e o desastre nuclear de Fukushima, o Japão iniciou um dos projetos de engenharia mais ambiciosos da história moderna: a construção de uma imensa barreira de proteção costeira com aproximadamente 400 quilômetros de extensão ao longo de sua costa nordeste, composta por enormes muros de concreto que chegam a atingir até 15 metros de altura em alguns trechos. Essa megaestrutura, que custou dezenas de bilhões de dólares, utiliza tecnologia de ponta incluindo sistemas de comportas automatizadas e sensores sísmicos, porém divide opiniões no país entre aqueles que celebram a segurança proporcionada e os que criticam o impacto ambiental e a alteração da paisagem costeira, enquanto especialistas internacionais estudam o modelo japonês como referência para países vulneráveis a tsunamis, debatendo sobre a eficácia real dessas estruturas físicas versus sistemas de alerta precoce e planejamento urbano adequado.

snippet.title: OURO de TOLO: como a pirita ENGANOU exploradores
snippet.description:
Você já ouviu falar no ouro de tolo? Esse mineral brilhante já causou muita confusão na história — enganou exploradores, provocou tretas em corridas do ouro e até recebeu o nome de “Fool’s Gold” em inglês. 

Conheça todos os livros do Manual do Mundo: https://www.amazon.com.br/shop/manualdomundo

Mas por que será que tanta gente confundiu a pirita com ouro de verdade? E mais: será que dá mesmo pra diferenciar os dois só olhando? 

No fim do vídeo, a gente vai colocar a pirita lado a lado com o ouro verdadeiro e você vai testar se consegue notar a diferença. Bora descobrir?
